consumer.faq.q001:
Charging points on site fall into three types — choose by how urgent your trip is and the charging power your vehicle supports:
DC fast chargers (typically 60–240 kW): feed high-voltage DC straight to the battery; usually 20%→80% in 30–45 minutes. Ideal for most battery-electric and fast-charge-capable plug-in hybrids.
Liquid-cooled ultra-fast chargers (360–600 kW): high-current liquid-cooled cables, thinner and lighter. With an 800V platform (e.g. Xpeng G9/G6, Zeekr 001/007, Li Auto MEGA/L high trim, Porsche Taycan) you can add 300–400 km in as little as 10–15 minutes.
AC slow chargers (7 kW): 220V AC converted onboard by the OBC; a full charge takes 6–8 hours — best while shopping, dining, or working nearby.
💡 Tip: DC and AC use different connectors (9-pin large vs 7-pin small). Check your vehicle's inlet before plugging in.
consumer.faq.q002:
Most partner stations include free or discounted parking while you charge:
Threshold: a single charging order meeting the basic requirement (usually ≥2 kWh delivered or ≥15 minutes of charging) grants 2 hours of free parking (see the station's posted signs for details).
Automatic validation: bind your real license plate under App → Profile → My Vehicles. After charging ends, the system pushes the waiver to the barrier gate automatically and you drive out without stopping.
Overstay: time beyond the free window is charged by the parking operator at its posted rates, settled directly by the barrier — it never appears on your charging bill.
💡 Tip: bind your plate before you arrive so you can leave without any wait.
consumer.faq.q003:
At stations that support reservations the rules are:
Hold time: pick a free charger marked as reservable, tap Reserve, and the platform locks it for you for up to 120 minutes; other users scanning it during that window are told it is reserved.
Fee: a small reservation deposit (typically ¥5–10) is charged per session.
Free cancellation: cancel within 10 minutes of booking and the deposit is refunded in full immediately.
No-show: if you have not plugged in within 30 minutes, the space is released automatically and the deposit is kept to compensate the station for the idle slot.
💡 Tip: plan your route so you arrive within the reservation window.
consumer.faq.q004: On-site assistance: contact our agents in the App chat or tell the on-site patrol staff — station operators will help reach the blocking vehicle's owner and have it moved.
consumer.faq.q005:
Amenities: on the station detail page in the App, the Facilities tab shows whether the site offers restrooms, a driver lounge, vending machines, free Wi-Fi, canopies and more.
Hours and gates: stations are either 24/7 or time-limited (e.g. some mall garages 07:00–22:00). Where a night barrier exists, the detail page marks Night Entry Guidance; at the gate, tell security you are there to charge and you will be let through.
Lounge access: at stations with a dedicated lounge, tap Scan to Open Door on the App's charging screen for free access to air conditioning and drinking water.
💡 Tip: if the barrier will not open at night, call the 24-hour station duty number posted on the charger body.
consumer.faq.q006:
Follow this standard sequence for a smooth start:
Park and power off: pull in squarely, shift to P, and switch the vehicle fully off.
Open the charge port: flip open the port cover (large opening for DC, small for AC).
Insert the connector firmly: take the gun off the dock, align it, push it straight in until it clicks — the mechanical latch must be fully seated.
Scan or tap: open the App or WeChat/Alipay, scan the QR code on the charger, choose a mode (e.g. auto full, by amount), confirm, then tap Start Charging.
Watch the start: the charger's indicator turns from blue (idle) to green (charging), and the App shows live kWh, power and voltage — you are charging.
💡 Tip: DC cables are heavy. Support the gun with one hand and push the handle with the other so the pins seat properly.
consumer.faq.q007:
Work through these four steps — most start failures clear quickly:
Step 1 – Is the connector fully seated? Unplug and check the gun head and the car socket for dirt, debris or water; then push firmly until you hear the click of the mechanical latch.
Step 2 – Was the emergency stop pressed? Check the red mushroom EMERGENCY STOP button on the front or side of the charger. If pressed, twist it clockwise so it pops back out.
Step 3 – Is the car fully off? Vehicle off, in P, lights and A/C off, doors unlocked — some models refuse charging while armed/locked in anti-theft state.
Step 4 – Scan again: wait 10 seconds and re-scan the QR code. If two attempts fail, the charger may have a temporary communication or hardware fault — move to the adjacent free charger; the fault is logged automatically.
💡 Tip: if several chargers all fail to start, the car's battery communication or OBC may be self-locked — power the car off completely, lock it, wait 5 minutes and try again.
consumer.faq.q008:
What it is: Plug & Charge (Autocharge) lets you skip scanning entirely. Plug in and the charger identifies your vehicle by its VIN, starts charging automatically, and bills your linked password-free payment method when you unplug.
How to enable: App → Profile → Plug & Charge → Add Vehicle. Enter your license plate and VIN (vehicle identification code) and make sure your wallet balance covers a charging session.
Off/unbind: lending the car or changing vehicles? You can switch the feature off or unbind at any time in the App.
💡 Tip: some older models or non-standard private-protocol vehicles cannot pass the VIN through automatically — check the vehicle compatibility list.
consumer.faq.q009:
Bind the card: App → Profile → Charging Card Management → Bind New Card; enter the 16-digit card number and the initial verification code printed on the back of the card.
Shared balance: after binding, the physical card draws directly from your App wallet balance or membership benefits — no separate top-up for the card.
Start by card: plug in the connector, then hold the card on the charger's RFID sensing area for 2–3 seconds; the charger beeps, recognises the account and starts charging.
Stop by card: when finished, tap the same card on the sensor again and the charger cuts power and settles the order.
💡 Tip: the physical card is ideal in underground garages with poor signal, or for older drivers.
consumer.faq.q010:
Do NOT yank it! The vehicle's anti-theft electronic lock or the charger's latch has probably not released. Try these in order:
Method 1 – Unlock repeatedly from the car (solves ~90% of stuck guns): on most models (Tesla, BYD, VW, Zeekr, Xpeng, etc.) the charge-port lock is linked to the door locks — press the unlock button on the key fob 2–3 times, or on the centre screen tap Stop Charging & Unlock Charge Port.
Method 2 – Push-press-pull: push the gun firmly into the socket with one hand (this relieves the latch), press and hold the micro switch on the handle with the other, and pull straight out quickly while holding it.
Method 3 – Pull the car's mechanical emergency cable: most EVs have a manual release (usually orange/yellow or marked with a plug icon) behind an interior trim panel in the boot near the charge port, or inside the port cover. Pull it gently to release the latch, then unplug normally.
Method 4 – Remote unlock by support: if nothing works, send the charger number in the assistant chat — support can push a remote unlock command to the charger or dispatch on-site staff.
⚠️ Note: brute force can break the socket's internal latch or damage the high-voltage communication pins. Idle fees caused by a stuck gun are refunded in full.
consumer.faq.q011:
An unexpected mid-session stop is normally one of the system's self-protection mechanisms doing its job:
Insulation protection: if the insulation impedance of the high-voltage loop reads low (especially in rain or humidity), the system trips within milliseconds to prevent leakage.
Battery over-temperature: in summer heat or during high-power charging, once the battery reaches its safety threshold the vehicle's BMS orders the charger to stop. Let the car cool for 10–15 minutes, then charge again.
Full-charge cut-off: some cars are set to stop at a target SoC (e.g. 80% or 90%).
Billing: after an early stop the system keeps the kWh delivered and settles normally; unused prepayment is returned to the original payment method. You can simply move to another charger.
💡 Tip: if charging stops after 1–2 minutes on multiple different chargers, have the onboard charger or high-voltage insulation inspected at your dealer.
consumer.faq.q012:
Real charging power is not the charger's nameplate rating — it is decided jointly by the battery's state and the charger's dynamic allocation:
Above 80% SoC – trickle phase: to protect cell life and prevent lithium plating, the BMS asks the charger to cut current sharply; power steps down (e.g. 80 kW → 15–30 kW). This is normal battery protection.
Dual-gun power sharing: on a twin-connector charger, if another car is charging next to you the power modules split evenly (120 kW → 60 kW + 60 kW); it climbs back automatically when the neighbour leaves.
Cold-weather protection: below 0°C battery activity drops; part of the power first heats the battery, and charging speeds up once the cells reach operating temperature.
Vehicle intake limit: some PHEVs and 400V-platform cars cap at 30–60 kW by design — even on a 480 kW ultra-fast charger they charge at the vehicle's own maximum.
💡 Tip: for daily top-ups, unplug at 80–85% — that is where overall charging efficiency is highest and waiting time shortest.
consumer.faq.q013:
Three safe ways to stop early:
App remote stop (recommended): on the charging screen in the App or mini program, tap the red End Charging button and confirm (payment password where applicable); power is cut and the bill is generated immediately.
Charger touchscreen: on the charger's display tap Stop Charging and confirm by scanning the on-screen QR code or tapping your card.
Car centre screen: in the vehicle's charging management page tap Stop Charging & Unlock Connector.
After stopping, wait 5–10 seconds for the relay's click, then release the handle latch, unplug, and return the gun to its dock.
⚠️ Note: never yank the gun out while charging — arcing can damage the pins.
consumer.faq.q014:
Yes, you can run the A/C: while charging you may stay in the car with power on and the air conditioning running.
Effect on charging: with the A/C compressor and other loads drawing power, the net power reaching the battery can dip by about 2–5 kW and a full charge may take slightly longer.
Safety: the vehicle's BMS coordinates the A/C load with the battery's fast-charge thermal management and has complete high-temperature protection — no harm to battery life.
💡 Tip: during extreme summer heat with cooling fans at full blast, waiting in the air-conditioned lounge is more comfortable and charges faster.
consumer.faq.q015:
Your total cost = electricity fee + charging service fee:
Electricity fee: follows the grid company's published time-of-use tariff (sharp-peak, peak, flat and valley periods).
Service fee: covers the station's operation, maintenance and equipment use.
Precise per-period billing: if a session crosses tariff periods (e.g. flat 11:45 → peak 12:30), the system splits metering exactly at the boundary: kWh from 11:45–12:00 are billed at the flat rate, 12:00–12:30 at the peak rate. The bill itemises kWh and unit price per period — we never bill the whole session at the highest rate.
💡 Tip: charging at night or early morning (usually 00:00–08:00 valley hours) is the cheapest.
consumer.faq.q016:
Idle (occupation) fees exist so a finished car does not block a needed charger:
Grace period: after charging ends (auto-stop or manual), you get 15–30 minutes to move the car free of charge.
Rate: once the grace period expires with the gun still plugged in, the fee accrues per minute at about ¥0.5–1.0/min (≈¥30–60/hour), capped per order per day (typically ¥100–200).
Reminders: the system sends several rounds of reminders by SMS, App popup and WeChat — near-full, session ended, 5 minutes of grace left, and when billing starts.
Stop condition: billing stops the moment you unplug and return the gun to its dock.
💡 Tip: if a stuck connector caused the idle fee, contact support — it is refunded in full.
consumer.faq.q017:
Refund timing depends on the payment method you used:
Top-up wallet (prepaid): funds are frozen at session start and the actual consumption is deducted when charging ends.
Platform wallet balance: actual costs are deducted at the end; the remaining balance can be withdrawn in full at any time via Profile → My Wallet → Request Refund, returning to the original payment account within 1–3 business days.
consumer.faq.q018:
How deduction works: at settlement the system automatically selects and ticks your single best coupon. One coupon per order; stacking is not allowed.
Restrictions:
Service-fee vouchers only offset the charging service fee, never the policy-regulated electricity fee.
Spend thresholds: some coupons require a minimum order (e.g. ¥5 off over ¥30) and will not apply below it.
Station/period limits: some coupons are valid only at specific stations or during designated valley periods.
Refunds: if an order fails and is refunded, any coupon consumed is returned to your coupon wallet within 10 minutes with its validity extended automatically.
💡 Tip: check each coupon's scope and expiry under Profile → Coupon Wallet before charging.
consumer.faq.q019:
Invoicing is simple and fully compliant:
Where: App/mini program → Profile → Invoice Management → Request Invoice, then tick the historical charging orders to invoice.
Types: both general VAT e-invoices and special VAT e-invoices (digital invoice format) are supported.
Contents and rates: per tax rules, invoices reflect the actual consumption split into Electricity (13% VAT) and Charging Service Fee (6% VAT).
Delivery: within two business days the e-invoice is emailed to you; PDFs can be previewed and downloaded any time from the invoice history.
Consolidation: tick multiple orders to combine them into a single invoice.
Amounts: only the cash actually paid is invoiceable — coupon deductions and marketing credits are excluded.
💡 Tip: corporate fleet users can pre-store their special-VAT-invoice credentials (tax number, bank, account) under Title Management for faster invoicing.
consumer.faq.q020:
Idle fees not caused by the driver are fully refundable:
How to appeal: App → My Orders → the charging order → Fee Appeal, or contact support directly.
Covered cases: the connector mechanically jammed after charging ended and the car could not be moved in time; the exit was blocked by illegally parked vehicles; an App or network failure prevented manual settlement.
Review and refund: once support verifies the charger's device logs, the wrongly charged idle fee is returned to the original payment channel within 1–24 hours.
💡 Tip: whenever device logs confirm a stuck gun caused by equipment fault, the idle fee is refunded 100%.
consumer.faq.q021:
If you were charged but no energy was delivered:
Express refund: for problem orders, contact support; once the delivered kWh are verified, an express refund is triggered and the money returns to the original payment method within seconds.
Coupon compensation: if the failed order consumed a coupon, it is returned automatically to your coupon wallet with its validity extended.
💡 Tip: watch for the refund notification from your WeChat/Alipay payment assistant.
consumer.faq.q022:
Metering compliance: every energy meter on an operating charger passes mandatory verification by the national legal metrology authority and carries a valid Mandatory Verification Certificate sticker on the body.
Why the numbers differ: the charger meters the total energy delivered from its side. Part of it is consumed en route — battery cooling pumps, cabin A/C, cable heating and AC/DC conversion losses (typically 5–10% combined) — so the charger's kWh read slightly higher than the net kWh the dashboard shows entering the battery.
Request a re-check: if you still doubt a specific charger, report a device fault in the App; operations will pull the order, re-verify the calibration and issue you an inspection report.
💡 Tip: before charging you can check the verification certificate number and validity on the charger body.
consumer.faq.q023:
Stay calm and proceed as follows:
Safety first: if the car hit the charger, switch off immediately and check the unit for tilting, exposed cables or sparks.
Photograph everything: from a safe distance capture the scene, the contact point, the plate number and the charger's serial number.
Notify the station: call the 24-hour operations hotline posted on the charger and report the incident.
Liability and insurance: for vehicle scratches or damage to public facilities, also call 122 traffic police for an accident liability determination; the platform will cooperate with police and insurers by providing station CCTV footage.
⚠️ Note: never tug on exposed or damaged cables — risk of electric shock.
consumer.faq.q024:
⚠️ If the charger or the vehicle's charge port shows smoke, sparks, a strong burning smell, or the car body feels live, follow these four steps exactly:
Step 1 – Evacuate now: everyone moves at least 10 metres away, upwind, into open space. Do NOT touch the car, the handle or the cables!
Step 2 – Hit the emergency stop: only if it is absolutely safe (no flames, no shock risk), smash the red EMERGENCY STOP button on the charger's front to cut the high-voltage input. If fire has started, do not approach!
Step 3 – Call the authorities: for open flame call the fire brigade (119) immediately and state that an EV battery/charger is burning; call the station's 24-hour emergency line (12306111) to have the unit de-energised and locked out.
Step 4 – No improvised rescue: burning traction batteries need sustained large volumes of water or dry-powder extinguishers — untrained persons must never pour water on a live high-voltage system.
⚠️ Note: never touch possibly live equipment — life safety always comes first!
consumer.faq.q025:
Outdoor chargers meet IP54-or-better rain and dust protection, but in severe weather follow these rules:
Standing-water red line: if water reaches half the wheel-hub height or approaches the charge inlet, do NOT charge — water conducts.
Keep rain out: when plugging or unplugging in the rain, shield the connector and the socket with an umbrella or your body; never let rain pour into the inlet. Check the gun head for water and dry it before inserting.
Thunderstorms: during yellow/orange lightning alerts avoid open-air ultra-fast charging; prefer underground stations.
No makeshift cables: never run extension-lead 'flying leads' outdoors in rain or snow.
💡 Tip: inspect the cable's insulation for cracks or damage before plugging in; if damaged, stop and report it.
consumer.faq.q026:
Prefer shaded spots: at midday in summer pick underground or canopy-covered bays to keep direct sun off the battery.
Rest after hard driving: after highway or spirited driving the battery is already hot; wait 5–10 minutes with the car off so the cooling loop dissipates heat before fast charging.
Leave the car while charging: DC charging means high voltage, high current and loud cooling fans — wait in the air-conditioned lounge or the mall instead of sitting in the car.
Stop at 80–90%: in high heat avoid repeatedly charging to 100%; staying at 80–90% markedly slows high-temperature cell ageing.
💡 Tip: if you smell burning or hear continuous loud buzzer alarms from the car, stop charging immediately and move away.
consumer.faq.q027:
Change phone number: Profile → Settings → Account & Security → Change Phone Number; verify with the SMS code sent to the old number, then enter the new one. Orders, points and wallet assets are preserved.
Forgot password: on the login screen tap Forgot Password, enter your registered phone number and set a new login and payment password via the SMS code.
Account deletion: submit under Settings → Delete Account. If a withdrawable balance remains, refund it first — otherwise the assets are cleared; deletion completes after the refund with data anonymised.
💡 Tip: invoice records cannot be restored after deletion — issue and export any invoices you need first.
consumer.faq.q028:
Assistant plus human: the intelligent assistant answers instantly, 24/7.
One-tap transfer: for complex issues or if the automated answer does not satisfy you, type human agent in the chat or tap Transfer to Human at the bottom.
Human service hours:
Online text support: 24/7.
Telephone hotline (12306111): 24/7 for urgent faults, on-site safety incidents and dispute appeals.
